newsitem.title: USA: D.C. commission extends PEPCO, BG&E merger hearing.
newsitem.headline: D.C. commission extends PEPCO, BG&E merger hearing.

text.p: District of Columbia Public Service Commission Friday extended hearings on the proposed $3 billion merger of Potomac Electric Power Co with Baltimore Gas and Electric Co for another five days.
Hearings will continue Feb 27-28 and March 3-5, or as long as it takes to address all 13 issues raised in the merger case, a commission official said.
As of Friday, after almost four days of testimony the commission had addressed just two out of the 13 issues -- merger benefits and economic development in the District.
Other major issues still to be discussed included the effect of the merger on nuclear power, rates and competition.

PSC chairwoman Marlene Johnson and consumer groups repeatedly raised questions about potential rivals to the merged company, Constellation Energy Corp, looking to make sure that it would not have too much control over the market.
PEPCO and BG&E have said they wanted to merge in order to cut costs and position themselves for a more competitive power market, but they have not specified who else they expect to supply their area.
"We're trying to identify the competitive environment Constellation is going to operate in," Johnson said Thursday.
The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission last year raised similar concerns, and has yet to give its approval.
The companies are aiming to complete the merger this spring.
